# CourtLine Android 1.0.21: trusted LAN reconnect

Requires Backend 0.36.0-test.51 or later for secure reconnection. Existing legacy connections remain compatible. Physical network-change acceptance is still pending.

## Behavior
- Try the saved Backend address first.
- After a network/TLS transport failure, an already securely trusted Companion can look for the same Backend using DNS-SD (`_courtline._tcp`) on the active Wi-Fi/Ethernet network. No IP sweep or port scan.
- Ignore other Backend IDs, public/off-subnet endpoints, duplicates, VPN routes, stale callbacks and changed networks. At most eight candidate services, six seconds discovery, eighteen-second candidate budget, sixty-second cooldown. Secure HTTP exchanges have total-request cancellation deadlines.
- Before transmitting any device credential, require the exact leaf certificate SHA256 fingerprint trusted from the physical QR, then verify Backend UUID via `/api/server-identity` over that TLS connection. Never use advertised fingerprints as trust; no pinned-to-HTTP fallback. Stale credential origins fail closed rather than falling through to system PKI.
- Reopen the existing family as Companion. Only on successful verified reopen save the new address and trust together. Rehydrate the UI bridge after generation changes. No new enrollment, PIN resets, command replay, or recovery from revoked access.
- Existing unpinned HTTP registrations continue unchanged until a one-time trusted Secure Reconnect QR scan. That scan keeps registration and checks existing access. Fresh secure enrollment remains Companion-only; Control permission and individual PIN remain separate.
- Failed warm Companion reads can reverify on a later poll. Active Control is not automatically downgraded just because the app backgrounds or temporarily loses connectivity. For relocation while in Control, restart into Companion/reconnect; fully automatic same-Control-session roaming is not implemented.

## Migration / acceptance
1. Update Backend and Android together, retaining app data.
2. Existing device: Options > Pair Device > scan **Secure Reconnect** from the same Backend computer; confirm the trust prompt. Do not scan installer QR or fresh enrollment unless deliberately creating a new registration.
3. Verify the device remains the same record, name/PIN/permissions unchanged. It starts Companion after reconnect.
4. Move both PC and tablet to another shared network, restart Android, and verify saved-first timeout then pinned discovery finds the same Backend.
5. Check multiple Backend computers, revoked devices, cancellation, offline networks, and firewall/router multicast restrictions on real hardware.

## Test boundaries
All 58 non-browser checks passed before the final IPv4/cooldown-only hardening; affected discovery/TLS/integration tests were rerun on final source. Original Android signer and manifest identity preserved. JavaScript syntax checks passed. Native build compiled successfully. Browser visual regression cannot launch in this cloud due socket restrictions; no physical Android DNS-SD/camera/LAN acceptance claimed.

Real JVM tests exercise the shipped certificate verifier against TLS sockets: wrong pin receives no HTTP request/bearer, correct pin works with changed LAN hostname. Pure Java request-admission tests reject stale origins/HTTP downgrade. Actual Backend51 HTTPS integration checks two devices, same-family reopen, revocation isolation, wrong pin, and local-admin route denial. Android DNS-SD code runs against explicit API stubs for network confinement, duplicate candidates, service limits, cancellation and changed-route behavior. These are not hardware discovery tests.

Certificate renewal: a same-Backend Secure Reconnect QR can replace an expired/renewed certificate only after a dedicated explicit confirmation, pinned identity verification, and successful existing-device reopen. Discovery cannot silently rotate certificate trust.
